summary: Batch function-call requests lead to duplicate and out-of-order webhook side-effects when proxy rewrites idempotency header and SDK retries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicates and reordering of webhook side-effects when they send a single batch function-call request via the Python SDK. The customer uses per-action idempotency tokens in each function invocation within the batch. Their on-prem load balancer inserts/rewrites a header (X-Req-Id) for tracing which appears to be colliding with the SDK-sent Idempotency-Key header in transit (header name normalization), causing our gateway dedup layer to see truncated or normalized idempotency values.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate webhook posts for the same logical action (financial transactions) seen by the customer's downstream system.
- Out-of-order processing observed because their downstream dedup expects monotonic sequence numbers encoded in the idempotency token.
- Customer is on a Private deployment with strict audit requirements; duplicates create compliance and reconciliation work.

Environment:
- Customer: FinOptix (Private deployment)
- Region: eu-west-1
- SDK: python-redwood v1.6.3 (sync batch funcall API)
- Gateway: Private control plane behind customer LB (F5) that rewrites X-Req-Id
- Model used: redwood-gemini-1 (function-calling enabled)

Expected behavior:
- Each logical function-call in a batch should be deduplicated using the per-action idempotency token sent by the SDK. Retry semantics should not produce duplicate side-effects.

Actual behavior:
- On transient 429/503 responses the SDK retries the entire batch (per SDK retry policy). Because the LB rewrites headers and lowercases/truncates long header values, the gateway dedup layer receives idempotency tokens that collide across actions or are missing sequence suffixes. This leads to both duplicate invocation delivery and reordering at the downstream webhook consumer.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided request/response traces and webhook payloads (sanitized) attached to ticket.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure Python SDK v1.6.3 to send a batch of 3 function-calls in a single request, each with a per-action idempotency token (format: txn-<unique>-seq-<n>).
2) Put a proxy/load-balancer in front of control plane that rewrites X-Req-Id and normalizes headers (lowercase policy, max header length 64).
3) Simulate transient 429 on the first attempt to force SDK to retry whole batch.
4) Observe webhook receiver receiving duplicate posts and sequence numbers missing or duplicated.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) Load balancer normalizes/truncates Idempotency-Key header, dropping sequence suffix. 2) SDK retry policy retries whole batch, so when header is changed in-transit dedup keys collapse across multiple actions. 3) Customer's downstream dedup expects full token+sequence; when sequence removed, multiple actions collapse into same logical id.

Checks performed:
- Verified SDK sends per-action idempotency tokens in payload and also sets Idempotency-Key per action metadata (customer uses header mapping).
- Replayed request against internal staging with header length limits and reproduce truncated token behavior.
- Reviewed gateway dedup logic: dedup uses header value normalization (lowercase) and first 64 chars of value for index key (matches symptoms).
- Confirmed customer LB policy rewrites X-Req-Id and enforces 64 char header limit; it also lowercases header names and merges duplicate headers.

Interim conclusion: multiple issues combine (per-action idempotency in payload + header mapping + LB header rewrite + whole-batch retry) leading to collapse of distinct tokens into identical dedup keys and out-of-order side effects.
resolution:
Workaround (applied):
1) Customer has disabled header mapping on their LB for Idempotency-Key and configured passthrough for our Idempotency-Key header.
2) Advised to upgrade to SDK v1.7.0 (patch pending) that changes default retry behavior for batch funcalls to per-action retry where possible and includes token-hint metadata to avoid relying on header-only dedup.
3) Short-term: customer switched to send single action per request for high-value transactions until fix deployed.

Planned fix / follow-ups:
- Engineering will: (a) add server-side acceptance of idempotency in payload for batched funcalls rather than relying solely on header, (b) log full idempotency token before normalization to aid future debugging, (c) add a warning in private-deploy docs about LB header rewrite risks.
- Rollout plan: patch in next private control-plane release (v4.12.1) targeted 2026-03-18; advisory and upgrade notes to customer prior to rollout.
- Postmortem: produce short incident note and update runbook with LB config checklist.
